name: Kolsassberg
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain hamlet above Kolsass, featuring traditional farms and idyllic tranquility away from the main roads.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kolsassberg is a sun-drenched mountain village in the Tyrolean Unterinntal, perched on an idyllic scenic plateau on the northern slopes of the Tux Prealps just south of Kolsass. The municipal territory extends from an altitude of around 906 metres in the main village up to alpine peaks exceeding 2,500 metres. Home to approximately 850 residents, Kolsassberg is defined by its peaceful setting away from transit routes, traditional mountain farmsteads, and commanding panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley towards the jagged limestone crests of the Karwendel range. A tranquil retreat for nature enthusiasts, Kolsassberg is an insider tip for hikers and outdoor lovers year-round.

History

Permanent settlement of Kolsassberg began during the High Middle Ages through coordinated forest clearing on the mountain flanks and the establishment of dairy farms known as Schwaighöfe. The village's fortunes were intimately intertwined with copper and silver mining in the Kolsass valley and nearby Castle Rettenberg, which held strategic significance under Emperor Maximilian I and Florian Waldauf von Waldenstein in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. The miners and highland farmers formed a distinct community, culminating in Kolsassberg's establishment as an independent municipality in 1637. Many traditional wooden farmsteads survive today, showcasing authentic Tyrolean agricultural architecture spanning multiple centuries.

Getting There

Travel to Kolsassberg is via the Inntal valley corridor. By car, leave the A12 Inntal Autobahn at either the Wattens or Vomp exits, continuing along federal road B171 to the valley village of Kolsass. From there, the well-maintained Kolsassberg regional road (L333) winds upward in a few gentle hairpin curves onto the plateau. Train travelers arrive at Fritzens-Kolsass railway station, where regular regional buses operated by the Tyrol Public Transport Network connect directly to Kolsassberg. Hikers and mountain bikers can also ascend via signposted forest tracks from neighbouring villages.

Tips

A premier hiking destination is the historic ruin of Castle Rettenberg on the border with Kolsass, accessible via an enchanting forest path. During summer, Kolsassberg serves as a gateway to alpine excursions into the Tux Prealps, such as scenic hikes via the Innerst trail hub to the Weidener Hütte at 1,799 metres and onwards to the Rastkogel summit (2,762 m). In winter, the village transforms into a family-friendly haven with the Knappenlift and Hoferlift tow systems offering relaxed skiing for children and beginners, alongside groomed toboggan runs. After an active day outdoors, the traditional Hofer Stubn inn welcomes guests with hearty cuisine on its panoramic terrace.
